args.prompt: One continuous cinematic architectural take, slow and stabilized. In the first half of the shot the camera stays in the open floor space beside the bed and arcs gently to the left, holding a clear unobstructed wide view of the bedroom; nothing large passes across the foreground and the camera never brushes past curtains, columns or wall panels. It rotates slowly until the black cylindrical wood stove beside the tall black-framed windows settles into a flattering three-quarter view, with the forest windows and part of the bedroom still in frame. Throughout this first half the firebox is completely dark, cold and unlit, with no flame and no glow at all. Only in the second half of the shot, once the stove is already clearly framed and the camera has almost stopped, does a single small flame flicker to life on the logs behind the closed glass door, then grow slowly and steadily into a warm wood fire, its amber light gradually building on the black stove body and the stone floor. The flames stay entirely inside the stove behind the glass. Level horizon, natural parallax, gentle ease-in and ease-out. Daylight and the rest of the room's lighting stay constant. The stove keeps its exact shape, glass door, flue pipe and position. The ceiling-mounted television stays folded flat against the ceiling. No smoke in the room, no sparks, no fire outside the stove, no people, no text.
